message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate the report against rubric criteria.

C1 Introduction: Several ethical issues identified (test coverage driven by calendar, data loss treated as harmless, conflict of interest, no disclosure), links to engineering design ("Engineering design always trades quality against cost and time"), context in engineering organisations (release cadence, management, commercial pressure), stakeholders table with interests and decisions. Excellent. 10.

C2 Balanced Discussion: Arguments for shipping (Stalk, competitor, revenue, learning, no product defect-free) and against (WannaCry, Therac-25, EA code, Pentium, VW). Conclusions with recommendations for multiple stakeholders (Rachel, management, health dept, chip supplier, engineers). Excellent. 10.

C3 Compelling argument: structure logical, arguments support conclusion, systematic understanding for all stakeholders. Excellent. 10. Could be 8-10. The report is well structured, conclusions supported. I'd give 10 or 9 (whole numbers only; levels are 10, 8, 6...). So 10.

C4 Research and evidence: references [1]-[8], quantitative evidence (81 of 236 trusts, 19,000 appointments, $475M, $4.3B, six patients), qualitative (code of ethics). Four external case studies. Excellent. 10.

C5 Structure, format, language: abstract, intro, body, conclusion, recommendations; two tables and one figure; fluent writing; consistent IEEE referencing; ~word count? Let me estimate. The body seems around 1400 words; likely within limit. Language fluent. Excellent. 10.

Minor technical issues: WannaCry — "at least 81 of 236 hospital trusts" — NAO reported 80 out of 236 trusts affected (actually NAO says 80 trusts, 603 primary care organisations). Some sources say 81. Minor. The report says WannaCry "no medical device malfunctioned" — true. Therac-25: "six patients received massive overdoses" — correct (six accidents, three deaths; some overdoses not fatal). Actually six accidents, patients received overdoses, three died. Fine. Intel Pentium: $475 million charge — correct. VW $4.3 billion — correct.

The figure is a clear flowchart — good.

Word count: should check 1500 max for intro through conclusion. Intro ~450 words, discussion ~900, conclusion ~130, plus "most ethical path" 160. Might be around 1500-1600. Hard to say; possibly slightly over. I won't penalize heavily; could mention as potential issue. Actually let me estimate more carefully.

Intro: ~430 words. Arguments for shipping: ~230. Against: ~430. How should Rachel decide: ~250 plus table. Most ethical path: ~180. Conclusion: ~140. Total ~1660. Possibly over the 1500 limit. That's a potential issue worth flagging as technical issue but not a rubric criterion directly. I'll note it as a possible issue.

Also the "Most Ethical Path" section under body is fine.

Requirement coverage all met.

Overall.
